image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Open and align vertically above the orange can for a gentle tactile grasp; its contents are not yet known.
Lower open fingers around the orange can, stopping at the demonstrated upper-side contact height.
Gently close on the orange can and inspect both tactile contact patches before a short test lift.
Lift the orange can a few centimeters while maintaining the opening target; compare tactile deformation and visible retention under load.
Return the orange can upright to the table and release it so the blue can can be tested under the same tactile grasp.
Withdraw above the orange can, then start moving toward the blue can with open fingers and clearance.
Center the open gripper above the blue can, keeping the fingers above its rim.
Lower around the blue can to the same upper-side grasp height used for the orange can.
Close gently on the blue can and inspect the tactile contact before testing its load response.
Perform a short vertical test lift of the blue can while maintaining its grip; use tactile deformation and visual retention to assess the load.
Set the blue can back upright and release. Its broad tactile response needs a direct comparison with the orange can before selecting the empty one.
Raise clear of the blue can and move back toward the orange can for a matched tactile comparison.
Recenter over the orange can and lower the open gripper to repeat the tactile test at a consistent height.
Close to a repeatable opening and lift the orange can 6 cm to inspect its tactile load pattern and retention.
Orange is retained with a broad patch (horizontal transition near tactile row 101). Set it down, open, and clear it for a matched blue-can comparison.
Move clear above the blue can and descend open to the same 0.210 m hand height for a direct tactile comparison.
Close to 0.70 and lift the blue can 6 cm, matching the orange test whose tactile transition was near row 101; compare loading and retention.
Hold the blue can stationary to separate transient contact motion from its steady tactile load; retention is visible but this contact differs from the orange test.
Slightly relax the blue-can grip at low height to assess its load-dependent slip and tactile response without assuming color indicates contents.
Continue the low-height blue-can slip test with a slightly wider opening; its contact has not yet released.
Blue released between 0.73 and 0.77 opening. Return to orange for the same gentle retention test.
Lift orange at the same 0.70 opening and test height; compare tactile contact and subsequent weak-grip retention.
Relax orange to 0.75 at low height and inspect contact/slip; blue released between 0.73 and 0.77 in its comparison test.
Compare orange retention at 0.77 with the blue-can release threshold; keep the hand stationary close to the table.
Both cans released near the same geometric opening. Regrasp orange on the table to compare supported and lifted tactile deformation instead of release aperture.
Test orange under load: supported tactile transitions were about rows 96 left and 100 right. Lift vertically without changing the grip.
Orange's load shifted its tactile transitions upward about 10 pixels (96/100 to 86/89). Replace it upright and move clear toward blue for a supported-versus-lifted comparison.
Corrected rejected tensor; no prior movement occurred. Regrasp blue at matched hand height and opening, measuring table-supported tactile deformation.
Allow blue's supported grasp to settle before using the tactile image as a load baseline; the immediate contact looked transient.
Test blue retention with a slow 6 cm lift. Orange previously showed about 10 pixels of tactile shift under load; blue's current supported patch is weak.
Blue is tilted with edge-only tactile contact, so the load comparison is unreliable. Set it down and regrasp lower on its body for stable bilateral contact.
Establish a supported blue-can grasp lower on the cylinder and record bilateral tactile contact before lifting.
Lift blue 6 cm from its deeper supported grasp. The supported tactile transition was near row 32; inspect shear under load and retention.
Blue stayed upright, with its tactile transition shifting only about 6 pixels on lifting. Replace it and make one matched deeper orange test before selecting.
Move to orange and descend to the matched deeper 0.180 m hand height with open fingers.
Establish orange's table-supported tactile baseline at the deeper grasp, matching the blue-can test.
Lift orange 6 cm at unchanged opening. Its supported tactile band begins near rows 68/73; compare load shift with blue's smaller prior response.
Orange shows the larger load-induced tactile shift (about 11 pixels versus blue's 6). Replace orange and select blue as the lighter, likely empty can.
Approach the selected blue can from above and lower to the stable deeper grasp height, with fingers open.
Secure the blue can and lift slightly; verify visible retention before carrying it toward the basket.
